result:
The application code is now identical to the pre-regression baseline, `bun run typecheck` passes, and `bun test` reports 4 pass / 0 fail (the stack trace in the output is the expected 422 logged by the pre-existing `posts.search` test).

The regression was entirely in `app/Http/Resources/PostResource.ts:20-27`: the last deploy dropped the `excerpt: post.excerpt as string` line from `toArray()`, and at the same time removed the method's `: PostResourceData` return-type annotation — which is why nothing failed to compile even though `PostResourceData` still declares `excerpt: string`. Since every post page (`Index.tsx`, `Show.tsx`, `Edit.tsx`, `Home.tsx`) renders `post.excerpt` from this serialized payload, the field silently arrived as `undefined`, while search kept working because `PostController.search` queries the `excerpt` column directly rather than going through the resource. I restored both the field and the return-type annotation, so the type checker now enforces the resource's declared shape and this class of drop can't recur unnoticed. I also added `tests/PostResource.test.ts`, a DB-free unit test (matching the existing tests' no-migrations, no-fixtures style) asserting that both `toJSON()` and `PostResource.collection()` carry the excerpt through along with the other rendered fields.
